=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (multiple leaflets are clearly seen attached in pairs along the rachis in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaflets are densely arranged along the rachis, appearing crowded)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (the leaf is clearly divided into multiple distinct leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (a terminal leaflet is present at the apex of the leaf structure)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 11 (multiple leaves are visible; the most complete leaflets count is 11)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (leaflets are paired along the rachis)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): toothed (distinct, rounded teeth are visible along the margins)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaflets are elongated with the widest part near the base and tapering toward the tip)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (the tips of the leaflets come to a distinct, sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the base of the leaflets tapers to the attachment point)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with veins branching off to the sides)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible and spaced (distinct veins branch off the midrib at an angle)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): rugose (the leaf surface appears textured with sunken veins creating a wrinkled appearance)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (the surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): long (the rachis extending the leaflets is quite long)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the rachis appears round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stem appears green and flexible)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs are visible on the stem)
    19. Stem color: green (the visible stem is green)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears smooth)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the base of the petioles)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are present)
F. Notes: The leaflets exhibit distinct damage in the form of holes along the margins and irregularities in the leaf blade.
